s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness with ventricular tachycardia
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of dyspnea, palpitations, and lightheadedness
Markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function
key_facts: 66-year-old white man
Presented to the Emergency Department with abrupt onset of symptoms
Found to be in monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
Electrically cardioverted into normal sinus rhythm
Medical history includes cerebrovascular accident, Factor V Leiden and prothrombin gene mutations, hypertension, incidentally noted pulmonary nodules, and chronic kidney disease
Taking losartan and warfarin
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Initial laboratory studies were within normal limits
Coronary angiography ruled out ischemia
Electrocardiogram showed normal sinus rhythm without ischemic changes, but an epsilon wave in V1, a QRS duration of 140 ms, and T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular function and no valvular disease, but a markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Epsilon wave in V1, QRS duration of 140 ms, and T-wave inversions in leads V1–V5, with markedly dilated right ventricle and severely reduced systolic function

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pulmonary nodules and right ventricular dysfunction, with preserved left ventricular function

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia, with right ventricular dilation and dysfunction

shortlist.label: Right ventricular outflow tract tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia and right ventricular outflow tract dimension >32 mm

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular tachycardia with no clear ischemic or structural cause
